title: Climate change: from causes to everyday action
subtitle: an EAP course Academic Language and Communication | Your Name
issue: Scientific and technological progress has made daily life easier, but it has also increased greenhouse gas emissions, waste and pressure on natural resources.

columns.title: Causes
items: Burning fossil fuels for electricity, heating and transport
Deforestation and intensive farming, which reduce carbon storage
Industrial production and growing amounts of waste

columns.title: Effects
items: More frequent heatwaves, fires and floods (Shaw, n.d.)
Rising sea levels threaten low-lying coastal cities
Crop damage raises food prices (Vocal Media, 2025)

columns.title: What individuals can do
items: Use public transport, walk or cycle for short trips
Eat less meat and cut food waste

plan_title: My plan for the next month
plan_items: Take the bus or train to campus at least three days a week
Have two meat-free dinners a week
Write one paragraph a week using two sources
takeaway: Small, repeated choices by many people support the larger changes that governments and companies must make.
references: Shaw, N. (n.d.). What is climate change? [Reading]. an EAP course textbook, Chapter 5.
Vocal Media. (2025). Climate change: Its effects and solutions. [Reading]. an EAP course textbook, Chapter 5.
